population: Older adults from the Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study, Birjand, eastern Iran
conclusion: The T allele was carried by 8 of 227 participants (all heterozygous) and by none of the 40 aged 80-90, versus 1.39% and 4.65% allele frequency at 60-69 and 70-79 y; the authors read this as a non-significant trend toward an inverse link between the T allele and reaching advanced age. The paper's primary frailty analysis found no association (final adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.10-9.66, p = 0.98).
study_design: Cross-sectional genetic association within a population-based ageing cohort (PCR-RFLP genotyping)
statistical_test: Fisher's exact test, allelic, T-allele frequency across age groups 60-69 / 70-79 / 80-90 y
provenance_quote: the frequency of the T allele was numerically lower in the 80–90 years age group (0%) compared to the 60–69 (1.39%) and 70–79 (4.65%) age groups (p = 0.073)
